meta.title: Carthage Underfoot
meta.status: Checkpoint 1 — archive credits and descriptions are being verified
meta.honestyNote: Scanned artifacts are real documentation. The low-poly terrain, walls, columns, vegetation, placeholders, and artifact placements are modern abstractions, not archaeological reconstructions.

zones.name: Carthage Roman Temple Precinct
zones.blurb: Roman scans from Byrsa Hill and the villas are embedded in an interpretive North African temple precinct. The arrangement is not a measured reconstruction.

zones.name: Tunisia Details Court
zones.blurb: This separate study court presents downloaded Tanit XR scans from other Tunisian heritage sites. Their labels name their actual source places; they are not presented as finds from Carthage.

artifacts.title: Carved Architectural Block with Laurel Motifs
artifacts.shortLabel: A carved stone block with laurel patterns
artifacts.description: A decorated stone block featuring carved laurel patterns, once part of the Water Temple at Zaghouan — the sacred starting point of a Roman aqueduct that carried fresh water over 90 kilometres north to Carthage. The laurel motifs symbolised triumph, eternity, and divine favour in Roman tradition.
artifacts.context: This scan is from the Water Temple at Zaghouan, not from Carthage itself. It is placed here as an architectural study piece from the same Roman period.
artifacts.threat: The Water Temple of Zaghouan is an exposed outdoor site subject to weathering and gradual deterioration.
artifacts.interpretation: Its upright temple-wall setting is interpretive staging, not a reconstruction of the original temple setting.
